log.action: Race down the South Road toward the fighting.
log.narration: Turn 1 | Day 1, 7:02 pmThe screams pull you like a hook through the jaw. You break into a dead run down the South Road, gravel and ash spitting from your boots, chainmail slapping cold against your ribs with every stride. Through drifting smoke you see it: a merchant wagon overturned in the ruts, its ox down and screaming, oxen-blood black in the dusk light, and men in studded leather dragging a woman by her hair toward a second wagon caged in iron bars. One of them turns at the sound of your boots, and even at this distance you know that stance, that way of standing like the world owes him a debt. Your hand finds the hilt of your longsword before your mind has finished the thought, and something old and ugly wakes up in your chest.🔊………

log.action: Draw my longsword and advance cautiously.
log.narration: Turn 2 | Day 1, 7:03 pmSteel hisses free of the scabbard, and you close the distance at a wary crouch, sword low, eyes cutting the scene apart piece by piece. Three raiders in mismatched leather and stolen mail work the wreck, one wrestling the woman toward the cage-wagon, two more looting the merchant's crates with the lazy confidence of men who've done this a hundred times. The driver lies face-down in the ash, unmoving, a crossbow bolt jutting from his back like a black quill. Then the leader turns full around, firelight from the burning wagon catching his face, and your gut drops like a stone through water. You know that scarred jaw, that crooked grin. Theron Wyndfall. Older, harder, but unmistakably the same dog who used to crack the whip over your back in the pits.🔊………

log.action: Charge the slaver who turned to face me.
log.narration: Turn 3 | Day 1, 7:04 pmStrength attack rolld20: 17 -- hit"Well," Theron drawls, spreading his arms as if welcoming an old friend to supper, "if it isn't the North's own butchered ox, walked clean off my leash."You do not answer him with words. You answer with eight strides eating the ground between you and a downward cut aimed to open him collarbone to lung. He gets his blade up just barely, steel screaming on steel, and the impact judders up your arm into your teeth. Behind him the other two raiders freeze mid-loot, then start scrambling for weapons, and the woman by the cage-wagon wrenches free of her captor's slackened grip and bolts screaming into the smoke.🔊………

log.action: Spit a curse at Theron's old cruelty.
log.narration: Turn 4 | Day 1, 7:05 pmDexterity saving throw (Theron's attack)d20: 11 -- failed"Every scar you gave me, I remember," you snarl, circling him, sword weaving a slow arc between you. "Every night in that pit. I owe you for all of it."Theron only laughs, wiping a smear of blood from his lip where your first cut caught him, delighted rather than afraid. "Then come collect, ox," he says, and lunges, his blade darting for your ribs under the guard, quick as a snake for a man his size.The two thugs have found their nerve now, one circling wide to flank you, the other snatching up a hand axe from the wreckage and closing fast.🔊………

log.action: Press the attack, strike Theron again with Power Strike.
log.narration: Turn 5 | Day 1, 7:06 pmStrength attack rolld20: 19 -- hitPain howls up your side where his blade found meat, but you do not step back. You plant your feet and drive forward, putting your whole shoulder into the swing, steel screaming down in a arc meant to end him. He tries to twist away, but you catch him high on the arm, and the blade bites deep, grinding on bone, blood spraying black in the firelight.Theron staggers, snarling, his sword arm hanging half-useless at his side, blood sheeting down to darken the dust at his feet. But the flanking thug is on you now, hand axe whistling for your unguarded flank, and the other closes from your blind side with a short, wicked knife.🔊………

log.action: Cut down the axe-wielding thug before he closes.
log.narration: Turn 6 | Day 1, 7:07 pmStrength attack rolld20: 20 -- hitYou pivot on your heel, putting Theron at your back for one heartbeat, and meet the axe-thug's charge with a short, brutal cut aimed at his throat. He tries to bring the axe up to block, too slow, too late, and your longsword opens him from ear to collarbone in a spray that paints the ash red. He drops without a sound, axe spinning from dead fingers into the dirt.But Theron is not done. Even one-armed and bleeding, he lurches in low, driving his sword for your gut with the desperate strength of a man who knows he is dying, while the last thug's knife flashes for your kidneys from the other side.🔊………

log.action: Break away to keep both thugs in view.
log.narration: Turn 7 | Day 1, 7:08 pmDexterity saving throw (Theron's attack)d20: 9 -- failedDexterity saving throw (Thug's attack)d20: 16 -- successYou wrench yourself backward, boots skidding in the ash, opening space enough to see both blades coming. Theron's thrust goes wide, scraping a fresh line across your hip through the mail, and the knife-thug's stab catches only empty air where your ribs used to be. Now you stand with your back to the burning wagon, both enemies in front of you, and Theron's breath comes ragged, his good hand shaking around the sword's grip."Kill him, you useless dog!" Theron barks at his last man, voice cracking with pain and fury. "Valerius wants him breathing, not me bleeding out in the dirt for nothing!"🔊………

log.action: Finish Theron with a killing thrust.
log.narration: Turn 8 | Day 1, 7:09 pmThe name lands like a struck bell in your skull, Valerius, but there is no time to chew on it now. You drive forward past his failing guard, putting every pound of your weight behind the point of your longsword. It punches through his ribs and out his back, and Theron's eyes go wide and empty, the sneer frozen half-formed on his lips. He drops in a heap, sword clattering uselessly from his fingers, and the ash drinks his blood without ceremony.The last thug freezes, knife trembling in his grip, staring at his fallen leader with the wide, animal eyes of a man suddenly alone in the dark.🔊………

log.action: Turn on the knife-thug while Theron falters.
log.narration: Turn 8 | Day 1, 7:09 pmThe name lands like a struck bell in your skull, Valerius, but there is no time to chew on it now. You drive forward past his failing guard, putting every pound of your weight behind the point of your longsword. It punches through his ribs and out his back, and Theron's eyes go wide and empty, the sneer frozen half-formed on his lips. He drops in a heap, sword clattering uselessly from his fingers, and the ash drinks his blood without ceremony.The last thug freezes, knife trembling in his grip, staring at his fallen leader with the wide, animal eyes of a man suddenly alone in the dark.🔊………

log.action: Finish Theron before he can rally the thug.
log.narration: Turn 10 | Day 1, 7:09 pmHe's already finished. Theron Wyndfall lies broken in the ash at your feet, your blade through his ribs, the sneer wiped clean off his face by the same steel that once, in some other life, might have earned you a whip's stroke for insolence. There is nothing left of him to rally anything. Only the last thug remains, and he stands frozen a few paces off, knife shaking in his fist, torn between the courage to avenge his master and the plain animal wisdom that says the man before him has already killed two others tonight without slowing his breath."Gods below," the thug breathes, backing a step. "You're him. You're the one Valerius wants."🔊………

log.action: Turn on the knife-thug while Theron falters.
log.narration: Turn 11 | Day 1, 7:10 pmTheron does not falter. Theron is dead, and stays dead, spitted through the ribs in the ash where he fell. You turn instead on the surviving thug, sword still slick and dripping, and take one slow step toward him, letting the firelight show him exactly what he's dealing with. His nerve breaks like dry kindling. He flings the knife down into the dirt and throws both hands up, backing away so fast he nearly trips over the ox's carcass."I yield, I yield! Don't gut me like the fat one, I'll talk, I'll talk!"🔊………

log.action: Demand the thug tell me about Valerius.
log.narration: Turn 12 | Day 1, 7:25 pmYou cross the distance and haul him up by the collar, sword-point resting light against his throat, close enough that he can smell the blood still drying on your knuckles. The wind gusts past, thick with ash and burning wagon-wood, and somewhere behind you the ox gives one last shuddering groan before it dies. You want a name to hang a plan on."Talk fast. Where does Valerius keep his cages, and what does he want with me?"The thug's throat works against the blade before words come. He is a scrawny thing, younger than Theron, with a rat's darting eyes that keep flicking to the corpses like he expects them to sit up and correct him."Warehouse. Dockside, in Ashenveil, past the fish-markets, the one with the black timbers. There's a grate, iron, you have to say the words or the guards inside gut you through the bars. 'The King is bound.' That's the watchword. Kadrun Zethran holds that door, he's Valerius's dog, mean as a rabid wolf."He swallows hard, eyes darting to your sword arm."As for you... Valerius don't want you dead. Wants you dragged back breathing. Something about the brand, the old brand they put on you. Says it still hums with the god's voice, or some priest nonsense like that. I don't ask questions. I just fetch and carry."That word, brand, lands like a fist in your gut, old iron-scar heat prickling under your shirt where Valerius's mark was burned into you years ago in some pit you'd rather forget.🔊………

log.action: Order the thug to sit and keep hands visible.
log.narration: Turn 13 | Day 1, 7:30 pmYou shove him down onto a scorched crate, and he goes without a fight, hands raised high like a man surrendering to a hangman. The fire behind him is guttering to embers now, and the ash-wind picks at his hair, at the dead ox's hide, at the corpses cooling in the ruts. He sits there trembling, watching your sword hand instead of your face, which tells you he has survived violence before by reading exactly where the killing blow will come from."I'll sit. Gods, I'll sit all night if you want. Just don't let Kadrun know I talked."The ambush is over. Theron is ash and memory now, the wagon a blackened skeleton, and the road ahead splits three ways under a sky the color of a dying coal.🔊………

log.action: Bind the thug's hands and march him toward Ashenveil.
log.narration: Turn 14 | Day 1, 9:30 pmYou strip a length of harness-leather from the dead ox's traces and lash his wrists tight behind his back, cinching the knot with the brisk economy of a man who has tied up plenty of enemies before. He grunts at the bite of it but doesn't resist, doesn't so much as flinch when your knuckles brush old bruises he already carries from Theron's discipline. You haul him upright by the collar and point him south, toward the smear of torchlight where the High Gate waits."Walk. You so much as slow your feet, I'll drag you the rest of the way by your ankles."He stumbles into motion, casting one last look back at the wreckage, at his dead companions, at the life he's leaving behind in the ash. The wagon trail narrows behind you as the South Road opens wide and pale under the darkening sky, ash sifting down like the world's own grave-dust, and somewhere ahead the gates of Ashenveil wait to swallow you both whole.🔊………

log.action: March the thug south toward Ashenveil's docks.
log.narration: Turn 15 | Day 1, 9:50 pmThe road gives way to cobbles slick with soot, and the city rises around you like a wound that never closed, black granite and rotting timber crowding close, gulls screaming somewhere unseen over the stink of tar and dead fish. You march the thug through streets that thin and darken as you go, past shuttered stalls and doorways where hollow-eyed watchers pull back into shadow rather than meet your gaze. The dockside district opens ahead, cranes standing skeletal against the ash-grey dusk, warehouses hunched shoulder to shoulder like conspirators.Your captive slows, breath hitching, and jerks his bound chin toward a squat building ahead, timbers black as a rotted tooth, no windows, one iron-grated door."That's it. That's the warehouse. Kadrun's probably at the door right now. Please, please don't make me knock."🔊………

log.action: Push on through the High Gate into Ashenveil.
log.narration: Turn 16 | Day 1, 9:51 pm"You're already there, fool. Look around you."He flinches at the correction, eyes darting, and you realize the man's terror has scrambled his wits worse than his tongue. The High Gate is long behind you, its torches swallowed by the maze of the Low Quarter an hour past. Ahead squats the black-timbered warehouse itself, its iron grate the only door, and somewhere close a figure moves in the gloom before it, broad-shouldered, watchful, exactly the kind of dog Valerius would chain to a door like that.🔊………

log.action: Question the thug quietly about Kadrun and the watchword.
log.narration: Turn 17 | Day 1, 10:01 pmYou drag him into the black gap between two warehouses, out of sight of that iron-grated door, and press him back against damp planking. Your voice drops to something low and hard, meant for his ears alone."Kadrun. What is he, how many stand with him, and don't waste my patience lying."He swallows, eyes flicking toward the mouth of the alley like Kadrun might materialize from the ash-choked dark just from being named."Kadrun Zethran. Big bastard, wears a chain hauberk under his coat, carries a cleaver-sword near as long as my arm. He don't work alone, there's usually two, three others posted inside past the grate, but he's the one at the door, always. Mean as they come. You already know the words, I told you back at the crossroads. 'The King is bound.' Say it wrong, say it hesitant, he'll know something's off. He's not stupid, just cruel."He hunches lower, voice dropping to a whisper."You don't need me for this part. I've done what you asked. Please."🔊………

log.action: Whisper the watchword 'the King is bound' at the door.
log.narration: Turn 18 | Day 1, 10:01 pmDeception checkd20: 11 -- failedYou leave the thug bound and trembling in the alley's mouth, harness-leather cinched tight to a post, and step out alone into the open lane before the warehouse. The iron grate looms black and cold, and behind it stands a shape broad as a bull, chain hauberk glinting dull beneath a ragged coat, a cleaver-sword hanging from one fist like a butcher's tool. Small eyes fix on you the moment you clear the shadows, sharp despite the brutish set of his jaw.You lower your voice and let the words fall flat and practiced, the way a man says something he's said a hundred times before."The King is bound."Kadrun goes still. His eyes rake over you, up from your boots to the breadth of your shoulders, lingering too long on your face."Watchword's right enough. But I know most every face that walks this door, and yours ain't one I've seen. Master send a new man and forget to tell his old dog?"His free hand drifts, slow and deliberate, toward the grate's iron bar, ready to either haul it open or slam it shut.His eyes narrow further, and somewhere behind that grate you hear the scrape of a boot on stone, another body shifting to attention.🔊………

log.action: Approach the door alone and speak the watchword to Kadrun.
log.narration: Turn 19 | Day 1, 10:01 pmKadrun's hand stops on the iron bar, not pulling it, not yet, and his stare hardens into something closer to certainty than suspicion."No. No, I know that face now. Ash and fire take me, that's the Northlander. The one Master's been tearing the city apart looking for."He doesn't shout for help. He doesn't need to. His grin splits wide and ugly, teeth yellow in the gloom, and he hauls the grate wide with a shriek of rusted hinges, cleaver-sword coming up in the same motion."Master said bring you back breathing. Didn't say whole."Behind him two shapes peel off the warehouse dark, one hefting a spear, the other drawing a short, wicked blade, both moving to flank their captain in the doorway.The cleaver-sword hisses down at your skull, and the doorway erupts into howling steel.🔊………

log.action: Grab Kadrun through the grate before he can retreat.
log.narration: Turn 20 | Day 1, 10:01 pmStrength checkd20: 17 -- successYou lunge before the cleaver-sword finishes its arc, closing the gap Kadrun meant to keep, and your free hand clamps around the collar of his coat like a wolf's jaw closing on a deer's throat. He's heavier than he looks, chain hauberk grinding under your grip, but you haul him forward off balance, dragging him half through the iron grate into the open lane where his two dogs can't easily flank around him.Kadrun snarls, cleaver-sword scraping against the grate's frame as he fights the pull, boots skidding on wet stone. His momentum is broken, his footing gone, and for one heartbeat he's nothing but weight on the end of your arm, wide open."Get OFF me, you ash-blooded whoreson!"The two guards behind him hesitate at the doorway, spear and short blade half-raised, unwilling to strike past their captain's floundering bulk without carving him open first.🔊………

log.action: Fall back through the doorway to fight them one at a time.
log.narration: Turn 21 | Day 1, 10:01 pmDexterity checkd20: 14 -- successYou wrench Kadrun's collar hard and haul yourself backward through the grate's frame instead, dragging him stumbling with you into the narrow throat of the doorway, a space barely wide enough for two men shoulder to shoulder. The guards behind him curse and shove forward, but the doorway chokes them, spear and blade jamming against timber and iron, unable to bring both weapons to bear at once.Kadrun rights himself just as you release his collar, cleaver-sword whistling up in a backhand meant to open your throat. You catch the blow high on your own blade, steel screaming against steel, the shock of it running up through your shoulder.He's still standing, still snarling, but he's boxed now, his own men penned behind him in the doorway's narrow throat, unable to help without climbing over their captain's back."Clever dog. Won't save you."He sets his boots and comes on again, cleaver-sword rising for a second cut, chain mail rattling with the violence of the motion.🔊………

log.action: Wrench Kadrun fully through the grate as a shield.
log.narration: Turn 22 | Day 1, 10:01 pmStrength checkd20: 19 -- successYou seize the front of his hauberk with your off hand and haul with everything the North ever put in your back, wrenching him bodily through the grate's iron teeth and spinning him between you and the two guards jammed in the doorway. Chain links scrape and catch on rusted metal, and Kadrun roars in pain and fury as his own men's spear point skitters off his shoulder instead of your ribs.He's off balance now, thrown half against you, cleaver-sword arm pinned awkward and low, and the guard with the spear curses as he yanks the weapon back before it guts his own captain. You have one heartbeat where Kadrun is more hostage than foe, close enough that you can smell the tar and old blood on him."Fools, mind your aim, !"His cleaver-sword scrapes free of the tangle, and he twists in your grip, snarling, trying to bring the blade around into your side even as his own men shove forward behind him, boxed and furious in the narrow door.🔊………

log.action: Drive a Power Strike into Kadrun's chest before he swings.
log.narration: Turn 23 | Day 1, 10:01 pmStrength attack rolld20: 20 -- successKadrun's twist brings his ribs square across your blade's path, and you drive forward with everything your shoulders can throw into the steel."Die, then!"Your longsword punches through the gap in his hauberk where his arm had pulled the chain wide, biting deep into the meat below his ribs.He convulses around the blade, cleaver-sword clattering from fingers gone suddenly nerveless, and a scream tears out of him raw and animal, more shock than pain. Blood sheets hot over your knuckles, and behind him his two men freeze at the sound, spear and blade faltering in the doorway's narrow throat."You... gah... Master will peel the... skin from your bones..."He sags against you, weight dragging on your blade, still breathing, still dangerous, but broken open and bleeding out fast in the ash-choked dusk.🔊………

log.action: Drive a knee into Kadrun's gut to double him over.
log.narration: Turn 24 | Day 1, 10:01 pmMorale checkd20: 9 -- failedYou drive your knee up hard into the wound already opened, and Kadrun folds around it with a wet, choking cry, all the fight punched out of him in one convulsive heave. He drops to his knees on the wet stone, both hands clutching at the ruin in his side, blood pooling black beneath him in the gloom.The two guards behind him stare at their captain crumpled and gasping, and something in their stance breaks, spear point wavering, short blade dropping half an inch."Enough... enough, gods damn you, ENOUGH, "The spearman throws his weapon down with a clatter and backs against the warehouse wall, hands spread wide and empty, while his companion drops the short blade an instant later, both faces pale with the particular terror of men who watched their leader gutted in three heartbeats flat.🔊………

log.action: Wrench the blade free and let Kadrun drop.
log.narration: Turn 25 | Day 1, 10:01 pmYou wrench your longsword free with a wet, grinding pull, and Kadrun topples sideways into his own spreading blood, chest heaving in shallow, ragged gasps. He doesn't rise. He won't, not without a healer's hands on him soon, but for now the fight has left him nothing but breath and pain.The two disarmed guards press flat against the timber wall, hands still raised, eyes flicking between your bloodied blade and their fallen captain. Beyond the open grate the warehouse's interior yawns dark and silent, no torches lit, no voices raised in alarm, whatever waits within apparently deaf to its guard captain's screams. Kadrun's breath rattles wet in his throat, and his small cruel eyes fix on you with something between hatred and terror."Kill me clean, then, Northlander. Don't... don't let him have me back like this."🔊………

log.action: Order the surrendered guards to lead me inside.
log.narration: Turn 26 | Day 1, 10:06 pmYou turn on the two guards, blade still dripping, and your voice carries the flat certainty of a man who has already decided what happens to anyone who hesitates."Inside. Now. Lead, and you live to spend whatever coin he's paid you."The spearman's throat bobs, and he exchanges a glance with his companion before both nod, quick and jerky, the universal language of men who have decided their captain's fate is not one they intend to share. They edge past Kadrun's spreading blood, careful not to step in it, and shoulder the iron grate wider on groaning hinges."Don't kill us. We only stand watch, we don't go past the second row of crates, nobody does unless Kadrun sends for them, "The taller one falls silent as the dark swallows the doorway ahead, and past his shoulder you catch it: a low sound rising from somewhere deep in the warehouse's black gut, not quite a voice, not quite a chant, curling through the dust-thick air like smoke finding its way toward a fire.Kadrun's ragged breathing fades behind you as the two guards shuffle forward into the gloom, torches unlit, clearly unwilling to announce your arrival any louder than they must. The reek changes past the threshold, brine and rot giving way to something sharper, copper and something else beneath it, bitter, almost sweet, an alchemist's smell wearing a butcher's coat.🔊………

log.action: Grant Kadrun the clean death he's begging for.
log.narration: Turn 27 | Day 1, 10:07 pmYou turn back to Kadrun where he lies gasping in his own blood, and for a moment you look down at him without hatred, only the flat recognition of one fighting man for another's ruin. He meets your eyes and something like gratitude cracks through the pain on his face."Northlander... thank you.""Wasn't done for you."Your longsword falls once, clean and final, and the guard captain's fear, his pain, his master's leash on him, all of it ends together in the space between one heartbeat and the next.The two guards flinch at the sound but say nothing, understanding perhaps better than most what mercy looks like in a place like this. Behind them the warehouse's dark throat still murmurs its low, wordless chant, patient and undisturbed by the death of the man who kept its door.🔊………

log.action: Press deeper past the second row of crates.
log.narration: Turn 28 | Day 1, 10:17 pmKadrun lies still behind you, the killing blow already given, and you leave him to whatever cold reckoning waits for men like him. Ahead, the guards' shoulders stay tight with dread as they lead you past the second row of crates, deeper into the warehouse's black gut.The chant grows clearer now, though no clearer in meaning, syllables that scrape against the ear like they were never meant for a human throat. A greasy light bleeds out from somewhere past the crates ahead, sickly green, flickering unlike any honest flame. The taller guard stops dead in his tracks, sweat cutting pale tracks through the grime on his face."That's as far as I go. Please. That's the alchemist's light, and I've seen what happens to the ones who get too close to it."🔊………

log.action: Search Kadrun's body for keys or papers.
log.narration: Turn 29 | Day 1, 10:22 pmInvestigation checkd20: 16 -- successYou crouch beside Kadrun's cooling body, ignoring the guard's whimpered protest at your back, and go through him with the brisk, practiced hands of a man who has looted corpses before. A ring of iron keys comes off his belt, along with a folded scrap of vellum tucked inside his coat, ink smudged but legible enough.The note is short, written in a cramped, hurried hand, plainly meant for Kadrun's eyes alone. Deliveries to continue past dusk. The Alchemist's vats run day and night now; tell the men the smell means the work is close. Master says the Northlander is worth ten of any brand we've made. Bring him breathing or don't bring him at all.No signature, but you don't need one. The keys are heavy, cold iron, several teeth worn smooth from use, plainly meant for more than one lock deeper in this place.🔊………

log.action: Creep toward the green light to see its source.
log.narration: Turn 30 | Day 1, 10:22 pmDexterity checkd20: 17 -- successYou leave the guards where they stand, pale and shaking by the crates, and move alone toward that sickly green glow. The chanting swells as you close the distance, less a chant now than a wet, rhythmic muttering, dozens of voices layered thin over each other like water over stone. You round the last stack of crates low and quiet, blade ready, and the source of the light opens up before you.A wide chamber sprawls beyond the cargo, ringed with black iron vats taller than a man, each one bubbling with something that glows faint sickly green from within, casting long twisted shadows up the warehouse's rafters. Chained to iron rings along the far wall stand a dozen men and women, gaunt, slack-jawed, eyes rolled white, brands smoking faintly on bare shoulders and collarbones, the same mark seared into your own flesh years past. Between the vats moves a lean, stooped figure in an alchemist's leather apron, humming that same wordless chant as he dips a ladle into the nearest vat and pours something dark and glistening down a chained captive's throat.The captive convulses, back arching, muscles cording up thick and sudden beneath skin gone taut as drumhide, and a low animal groan tears out of a throat that sounds nothing like human pain anymore. The alchemist doesn't look up, doesn't break his tune, entirely absorbed in his work, and for the moment his back is turned and you remain a shadow among shadows at the chamber's edge.🔊………

log.action: Try the iron keys on the nearest crate or door.
log.narration: Turn 31 | Day 1, 10:32 pmLockpicking checkd20: N/A -- auto-successYou ease back from the vat-chamber's edge, leaving the alchemist to his grim work, and try the ring of iron keys against a stout, banded door set into the wall near the crates you'd passed. The third key grinds home and turns with a heavy clunk, tumblers old and thick with rust giving way under your hand.The door swings inward on a short storeroom, shelves lined with corked jars and clay vessels, each one holding the same dark glistening substance you watched poured down a captive's throat. Ledgers lie stacked on a low table, pages thick with cramped alchemical notation, columns of names beside columns of numbers, and one word repeated again and again in the margins in a hand pressed hard enough to tear the vellum: Chained.A second, smaller door stands at the room's rear, unlocked, slightly ajar, cold air seeping through the gap along with the faint, distant sound of chain dragging over stone.🔊………

log.action: Rush the alchemist before he notices me.
log.narration: Turn 32 | Day 1, 10:32 pmStrength attack roll (surprise)d20: 19 -- successYou leave the storeroom's grim ledgers behind and turn back toward the vat-chamber, boots silent on stone, blade already rising. The alchemist's back stays turned, hunched over his ladle, humming his wordless tune, utterly deaf to the death closing on him.You cross the last stretch of floor in three long strides, and he half turns at the scrape of your boot on grit, eyes going wide behind a stained leather mask. Too slow. Your longsword takes him under the jaw and up through the skull before the scream in his throat ever finds air, and he drops boneless among his own vats, ladle clattering into the green-lit muck.The chained captives along the wall stir at the sound, chains rattling, slack faces turning toward you with dull, drugged confusion rather than gratitude. One of them, a broad-shouldered woman with old scars crossing a fresh brand, fixes you with eyes that seem, for one flickering moment, almost lucid."You... you killed him. Gods. Now what happens to us?"Her voice comes out cracked and disused, but there's a spark in it, something that might be hope, or might be the same terrible hunger you can still feel humming faint beneath your own old scar.🔊………

log.action: Push open the rear door toward the dragging sound.
log.narration: Turn 33 | Day 1, 10:37 pmYou leave the branded woman's question hanging unanswered and cross toward the rear door, the one you'd found ajar off the storeroom, cold air still bleeding through the gap. The dragging sound draws closer as you push it wide, chain scraping stone in a slow, laborious rhythm, and beyond it a narrow passage drops away into deeper dark, walls sweating with damp, the warehouse's timber and stone giving way to something older beneath, foundation stones too large and too rough to be Ashenveil's own work.At the passage's end a single figure strains against a chain bolted to the wall, not a captive dressed in rags like the others, but a man in a fine coat gone filthy with grime, wrists raw and bleeding where iron cuffs have worn through skin. He looks up at your approach with wild, hunted eyes, and there is something in the shape of his face, something in the terror there, that strikes a chord of recognition you cannot yet place."You're not one of his.
